lines.text: Two ships start 127.5 kilometers apart and head straight toward each other.
One moves at 40 kilometers per hour, the other at 45. How far has the first one gone when they meet?
Forget the two separate trips. Together they close the gap at 40 plus 45, which is 85 kilometers per hour.
So they meet after 127.5 divided by 85, which is 1.5 hours.
In that time the first one covers 40 times 1.5, which is 60 kilometers.
When two things move toward each other, add their speeds. Follow for a new puzzle every day.

lines.text: Two frictionless ramps have the same height. One is steep, one is shallow. Two identical balls are released from the top at the same moment.
Which ball is moving faster when it reaches the bottom?
Lock in your answer. Now watch what actually happens.
They are moving equally fast, at 10 meters per second. The ball on the steep ramp just gets there sooner, after 1.3 seconds against 2 seconds.
The speed a ball gains depends only on how far it drops, because the height it loses turns into speed. Both drop the same height, so both end up equally fast. The steep ramp just gets there sooner.
Same drop, same speed. Only the arrival time differs. Follow for a new puzzle every day.

lines.text: Five identical steel balls hang in a row, touching. Two balls are pulled back and released. The collisions are perfectly elastic.
How many balls swing out on the other side?
Lock in your answer. Now watch what actually happens.
Two balls swing out, the same number that went in.
Equal balls swap speeds when they collide. So each hit passes the motion down the row, and the balls at the end leave with exactly the speed of the ones that arrived.
Same number in, same number out. Follow for a new puzzle every day.

The ball thrown up rises, stops, and falls back past the edge moving downward at its original speed. From there it is identical to the ball thrown down.

lines.text: The same pendulum is set swinging twice, once on Earth and once on the Moon, from the same small angle. On the Moon, gravity is about one sixth as strong.
Where does it swing slower?
Lock in your answer. Now watch what actually happens.
On the Moon. One swing takes about 6 seconds there, against about 2.5 seconds on Earth.
With weaker gravity, the pull back toward the middle is weaker, so each swing takes longer. Here it takes about two and a half times as long.
Same string, same bob, different world, different pace. Follow for a new puzzle every day.

lines.text: Two objects are dropped. The second one starts four times higher than the first.
How many times longer does it take to reach the ground?

The low one lands after 2 seconds, the high one after 4 seconds. Only two times longer.
A falling object keeps speeding up, so it covers the extra height quickly. Fall time grows with the square root of the height, and the square root of four is two.
Four times the height, two times the wait. Follow for a new puzzle every day.

lines.text: A gear with 21 teeth drives a gear with 14 teeth. Their teeth mesh with no slipping.
When the first gear makes one full turn, how many turns does the second gear make?
Lock in your answer. Now watch what actually happens.
The second gear makes one and a half turns.
In one turn, 21 teeth of the first gear pass the meshing point, so 21 teeth of the second gear move past as well. That is 21 out of 14 teeth, which is one and a half turns.
A smaller gear always spins faster. Follow for a new puzzle every day.

Neither. They swing at exactly the same rate, about 3.5 seconds for one full swing.
A heavier bob is pulled harder by gravity, but it is also harder to get moving. The two effects cancel exactly, so the mass makes no difference.

lines.text: 6 gears are meshed in a row, and their teeth do not slip. The first gear turns clockwise.
Which way does the last gear turn?
Lock in your answer. Now watch what actually happens.
The last gear turns counter-clockwise, the opposite way from the first.
Two meshed gears always turn opposite ways, so every mesh flips the direction. With 6 gears there are 5 meshes. 5 flips leave one flip over, so the last gear is reversed.
